speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Given your symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, I need to ask a few questions to narrow this down. Have you recently traveled to or lived in an area where tuberculosis is common?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Tuberculin_Skin_Test (Mantoux)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: No pulmonary infiltrates, cavitations, or lymphadenopathy suggestive of tuberculosis observed; normal lung fields. Tuberculin_Skin_Test (Mantoux): Negative (<5 mm induration).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing those results; the negative imaging and skin test make pulmonary tuberculosis less likely. Given your persistent B symptoms and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, have you had any recent infections, dental procedures, or exposure to individuals with cat-scratch disease?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning; the combination of B symptoms and abdominal pain suggests a systemic process beyond simple infection. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, or have you experienced any blood in your stool?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Ultrasound: Splenomegaly detected with slight abdominal distension; no focal liver masses or free fluid observed. Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal.
